approach: Docs-only change. Create docs/design/context-engineer.md (about 400 lines, no code): question-to-file map, mapping call, what exists today (built vs proposed, each with source), part 1 conventions table (every row ends with 'mechanism: <named measure>' or 'prose-only'), part 2 inputs, post-mortem as an extension of the existing introspection record, cadence, budgets, restructure queue, relations, alternatives, build plan. Append D130 (proposed) to docs/decisions.md in D129's format, add a CHANGELOG line under Unreleased/Changed, and add a short cross-reference in hestia.md section 8. Every figure cites a source or is labeled an estimate. Unbuilt parts (code-health check 5p65, Jev checks zc0v, requirements engineer BRIEF.md 4A) are marked proposed; the introspector is described as built.

decisions.choice: Confirm Hermes (context and handoffs) as owner of the craft, Hestia (knowledge, docs, tidiness) as keeper and sweeper. Hermes sets conventions and owns the post-mortem outcome; Hestia's sweep runs the recurring doc checks. Record the call after reading hestia.md, D127 and roles-and-ladder.md.
decisions.reason: BRIEF.md pantheon row gives Hermes 'context, handoffs'; hestia.md section 8 and D127 give Hestia knowledge and tidiness and keep her non-gating. Splitting craft (rules, what agents read) from upkeep (sweep for drift) fits both. The ontology.toml entry says Hermes the god and Hermes Agent differ; the doc says it means the pantheon role. If roles-and-ladder.md shows a conflict, the producer records the change instead.

rejected.why: hestia.md is already a ten-job sweep, not a craft owner; D127 keeps her out of gating.
No evidence needs one; Hermes's row covers it.
Part 1 (file size, doc shape) is what makes part 2 cheap; splitting loses the link.

decisions.choice: Each convention row has a measure, a threshold labeled estimate, and an enforcement label 'mechanism: <named measure>' or 'prose-only'. Measures that need the code-health check (5p65) or Jev checks (zc0v) say 'needs X, not built'. Built things (introspector: crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs, schema athena.introspection/1, defaults-loop.md 3.1-3.4) are cited as built. The requirements engineer is cited as proposed in BRIEF.md 4A, not built.
decisions.reason: Mechanism default and criterion 4 forbid assuming unbuilt things exist, and equally forbid calling built things absent (critic findings 1 and 3). Ownership split with the requirements engineer: it owns the spec content and the shared vocabulary's meaning; the context engineer owns their size, shape, index and whether agents read them within budget.

rejected.option: Specify the code-health check output as if it exists
rejected.why: Not in the snapshot; invents facts.
Criterion 1 requires one; label estimates and calibrate in build job 1.
It exists in code and docs (finding 1).

decisions.choice: The post-mortem extends the existing introspection record. Add the planning-stopped trigger beside rejected and failed, and a 'context that would have prevented it' field with fixed outcome classes (system-facts line, failure class, brief assembly change, vocabulary term, spec fix, none). No separate recorded step. Additions to a prompt set over 95% of budget must name what they displace.
decisions.reason: Introspection already fires on rejected and failed jobs and asks Jev the failure-class and is-repeat questions; a second step would duplicate triggers and records and break one fact in one place. The budget rule keeps additions trade-offs: reader is at 1997 of 2000 (system-facts budget line).

rejected.why: Duplicates triggers, failure classes and storage already in introspect.rs, records.md and steward.rs; two records would drift.
Grows unbounded, unread, and breaks one-fact-in-one-place.
The request includes rejected and planning-stopped jobs.

decisions.choice: Restructuring is queued as ordinary requests, never edited by the role. Each names the slipped measure; cap on open restructure requests (estimate 3); a split must be behavior-preserving with existing tests unchanged. gh.rs and produce_and_verify are named as first candidates only.
decisions.reason: Matches hestia.md's fixes-through-the-pipeline rule and D127's non-gating stance; splitting now is out of scope.

rejected.why: Gating belongs to another role and would stall urgent work.

decisions.choice: Cite figures by source and re-measure what the snapshot allows (gh.rs lines, produce_and_verify span, decisions.md line count, budget lines). Figures needing records/ (7 retries that lost verifier findings, planning-stop counts) are labeled 'stated by the request, not measured here'. State the decisions.md count at the base commit beside the request's 3,231.
decisions.reason: Evidence default; the snapshot has no records/ and decisions.md is already longer than 3,231 lines.

decisions.choice: Build plan of six jobs, each one producer run, each with behavior bullets that show a failing case first: (1) size-convention measure report on a fixture with a known oversize file; (2) question-to-file map plus index check that fails on an unindexed doc; (3) decision-log index and archive design with a link checker; (4) extend the introspection record with the planning-stopped trigger and the prevention field, tested through the existing introspection path, plus carrying earlier verifier findings into retries; (5) budget guard failing above 95% without a named offset; (6) restructure-queue filer with cap.

files.purpose: The design: mapping, what exists today, conventions with measures, part 2 and post-mortem as an introspection extension, cadence, budgets, restructure queue, relations, alternatives, build plan.
Append D130 (proposed) after D129 in the same format, with the separate-record alternative rejected.
One line under Unreleased/Changed naming the design and D130.
Short cross-reference in section 8 to the context engineer role; nothing else changed.

steps: Read BRIEF.md pantheon row (about line 597), line 912, section 4A (about line 1010) and the 2026-10-26 addenda; hestia.md in full; roles-and-ladder.md; requirements-map.md header; scope-guard.md roles section; ontology.toml Hermes entry.

Read crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs and docs/design/defaults-loop.md sections 3.1-3.4, plus the failure-class text in docs/records.md; note triggers, fields and the athena.introspection/1 schema.
Measure at base: line counts of gh.rs and docs/decisions.md, the produce_and_verify span, and the budget lines in the system-facts file; record each with its source.

Draft context-engineer.md with sections: question-to-file map; mapping call; what exists today (built vs proposed); part 1 conventions table, each row ending 'mechanism:' or 'prose-only'; part 2 inputs; post-mortem as an introspection extension; measures and cadence; budgets (95% rule); restructure queue and cap; relations including the ownership split with the requirements engineer; alternatives; six-job build plan with failing-case-first bullets; not measured.
Append D130 (proposed) to docs/decisions.md in D129's format, with 'separate post-mortem record' among the rejected alternatives.
Add the CHANGELOG line under Unreleased/Changed.
Add the cross-reference to hestia.md section 8.
Run grep -c 'mechanism:\|prose-only' on the new doc, then cargo test --locked and git diff --stat to confirm only the four doc files changed.

risks.risk: The doc invents facts about unbuilt things or denies built ones.
risks.mitigation: A 'what exists today' table gives each item a source file or 'proposed in BRIEF.md'; the producer reads introspect.rs, defaults-loop.md 3.1-3.4 and roles-and-ladder.md first.

risks.risk: The doc breaks its own conventions by being long.
risks.mitigation: Keep it near 400 lines with a question-to-file map at the top; state each fact once.

risks.risk: The decisions.md edit lands inside another entry.
risks.mitigation: Append after D129 at end of file; check heading order after editing.
Write no address or run-location words; run cargo test --locked.
Re-measure at base and state the base figure beside the request's figure.

demonstrations.method: Grep the part 1 table: every convention row (file size, function size, one concern per module, one fact in one place, question-to-file map, index) carries a measure, an estimate-labeled threshold and 'mechanism:' or 'prose-only'. Compare the row count with the label count.
demonstrations.observes: Each named convention row has all three fields and an enforcement label; a threshold spot-checked against gh.rs size.
demonstrations.fails_without: A row without a measure, threshold or label shows as a row with no match in the grep.

demonstrations.method: Grep for the headings of part 2 and the post-mortem: triggers (failed, rejected, planning-stopped), the question, the outcome class list and the displacement rule; read them.
demonstrations.observes: All five inputs (briefs, system-facts, failure classes, vocabulary, spec) are covered; the post-mortem names its three triggers, the question and a fixed outcome list.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the post-mortem section no outcome list exists to find.

demonstrations.method: Grep each figure (5,276; 724; 3,231; 1997; 7 retries; planning stops) and check a source path, budget line or 'stated by the request' beside it; re-measure gh.rs and decisions.md line counts via Read/Grep count.
demonstrations.observes: Every figure has a citation or label; records-only figures are marked not measured here; base decisions.md count is stated.
demonstrations.fails_without: An uncited figure is a defect.

demonstrations.method: Read the mapping and relations sections against hestia.md section 8, roles-and-ladder.md, requirements-map.md and BRIEF.md 4A; grep the doc for introspect.rs, athena.introspection/1, 5p65, zc0v and k67x.
demonstrations.observes: Mapping confirmed with reason; five relations stated; introspector cited as built, code-health check, Jev checks and requirements engineer marked as not built with their sources; ownership split with the requirements engineer stated; hestia.md has a cross-reference.
demonstrations.fails_without: A relation claimed without a source file, or the introspector called absent, shows in the grep.

demonstrations.method: Read the measures, cadence, budget and queue sections; recompute 1997/2000 = 99.85% and check the 95% rule and the cap of 3 each have a number and a cadence.
demonstrations.observes: Each rule has a number or period an outside reader can test against the budget lines and file sizes.
demonstrations.fails_without: A rule without a number fails the outside-reader check.

demonstrations.method: Compare the D130 headings and bullets with D129's; grep the build plan for 'Acceptance' bullets per job and check each names a failing case before the passing one; check D130 lists 'separate post-mortem record' as a rejected alternative.
demonstrations.observes: D130 is marked proposed in D129's format and appended after D129 only; six jobs each have behavior bullets; job 4's bullet exercises the existing introspection path.
demonstrations.fails_without: A bullet that only says a file exists is rejected on reading.

demonstrations.method: git diff --stat to list changed paths; grep CHANGELOG.md for the new line under Unreleased; run cargo test --locked for the boundary scan and budget test.
demonstrations.observes: Only the four doc files change; no .rs, athena.toml or defaults.toml; tests pass.
demonstrations.fails_without: A code or config path in the stat, or banned or email-like text, fails the criterion or the scan test.

open_questions: Whether the code-health check (5p65) and Jev checks (zc0v) landed after the base commit; the doc states interface assumptions only.
The 7 lost-verifier-findings retries and planning-stop counts come from the request or records/, which the snapshot lacks.
Whether thresholds (for example file over 800 lines, function over 100 lines) fit Athena's code; estimates until the first measurement job.
Whether roles-and-ladder.md contradicts the Hermes mapping; the producer reads it and records the call.
How the boundary scan treats the name Hermes; run the policy test.
